source.title: Tractable Sharpness-Aware Learning of Probabilistic Circuits
source.authors: Hrithik Suresh; Sahil Sidheekh; P. VishnuShreeramM; S. Natarajan; N. C. Krishnan

record.file_problem: The supplied text includes the paper and supplementary material; some equations and table content are garbled or flattened.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies sharpness and generalization-gap analysis to probabilistic circuits, a different model setting from the neural-network findings in the versions.
record.gate_note: The study measures Hessian-trace sharpness and overfitting in probabilistic circuits and reports effects of Hessian-trace regularization. Its sharpness measure is not the magnitude-aware perturbation measure specified in V7, and it does not test V1–V6 or V8. Cited findings about neural networks are prior work, not this study's results.
record.test_reason: No claim version is tested. The closest results concern unscaled Hessian-trace sharpness and likelihood gaps in probabilistic circuits. V7 concerns magnitude-aware weight perturbations in convolutional classifiers and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures. Changing both the system and the sharpness construct does not establish a T3 test of V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' empirical conclusion: their regularizer steers probabilistic circuits toward flatter solutions and reduces overfitting, especially with limited data. Held-out improvements are not universal; the binary benchmarks show slight average deterioration at high data fractions. The observed associations alone do not establish that sharpness causes poor generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines probabilistic circuits, including Einsum Networks trained with Adam and PyJuice HCLTs trained with EM. It studies Hessian-trace sharpness rather than the original versions' neural-network interventions or magnitude-aware perturbation measure.
record.method_sensitivity: The regularization gains vary with training-data fraction and dataset; the paper reports gains plateauing as data increases, with a marginal test-NLL drop (< 0.5%) at the highest data fractions. Regularization strength µ affects validation NLL, overfitting and sharpness; small µ ∈ (0, 0.1] captures most gains, while larger values yield marginal gains at the cost of slight underfitting.

fits_no_version.finding: Hessian trace rises alongside the training-validation NLL gap during EinsumNet training and aligns with larger relative likelihood gaps across HCLT latent sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested probabilistic circuits, unscaled Hessian-trace sharpness qualitatively tracks likelihood generalization gaps.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed regularizer improves average test NLL substantially at 1% data and usually lowers sharpness and overfitting. Benefits diminish with more data; binary benchmarks show a slight average test-NLL worsening at 100% data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hessian-trace-inspired regularization can improve probabilistic-circuit density estimation in low-data regimes, with diminishing or slightly negative held-out benefits at larger training fractions.

record.code_released: Code will be publicly released upon acceptance to ensure reproducibility.
record.problems: The correlation evidence is qualitative and does not quantify the association. The quantitative summaries average five runs but report no uncertainty intervals in the prose. Some table content in the supplied text is flattened or garbled. The study concerns probabilistic circuits rather than the neural-network settings in the claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Aggregate results from Tables 1 and 2 are recorded from the paper's prose because the flattened table transcription does not reliably preserve all aggregate values.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance performance under random labels.
Width beyond zero training error and its effect on held-out classification error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout effects on classifier test error, including dataset-size and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, classification generalization gaps among convolutional networks with similarly low training loss, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equal-sized random removals and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to the supplied claim versions; this does not deny the reported probabilistic-circuit findings. Using Adam without an SGD comparison does not test V4, and varying HCLT capacity without demonstrating interpolation does not test V2.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Generalization as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers compared with SGD or momentum SGD.
Large-batch training and its effect under epoch budgets.
Dropout and its effect on held-out error.
The specified magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness measure and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
